Question: Jessie J says ADHD can be a "superpower." Do you agree?
Answer: Yes. It can be. Let me explain it to you using Megatron from Transformers Animated as an example. While he does also show some weaknesses of ADHD, such as distractability (he gets distracted from the fact that he needs repairs ASAP because he saw a pocket bot and decided to look for the damn Allspark again, even though he’s in dire need of repairs) procrastination (he procrastinated his repairs because he got distracted) , and trouble prioritizing (he prioritized something very trivial over his urgent need of repairs) , and does have moments where he doesn’t think things through, such as forgetting to check why Starscream always keeps coming back from the dead, or forgetting to assign a Decepticon to supervise the professor he’s taking advantage of in the episode “a bridge too close” , and overloads a space bridge, causing disaster, but as for the positive traits of ADHD this Decepticon is showing, his joined up thinking allows him to see the bigger picture and think outside the box. No matter the setback, he always finds a future advantage in there and uses it as a learning moment for the future. His joined up thinking really saves his chassis many times in the show. No matter the setback, he’s got that ADHD typical optimism, and always bounces back, adjusts his metaphorical crown, and keeps pushing forward. He may have a stern outward demeanor, but his innate optimism always shines through. And his demeanor is so energetic and passionate, it’s contagious, enabling him to better manipulate others to his advantage. I really like this character, because Hasbro accidentally created a character who very accurately showcases ADHD and ADHD masking. Animated Megatron may outwardly have a stoic and calculating demeanor, but that’s because he’s masking his ADHD or lest his troops might question Megatron’s sanity and assassinate him. Yet, his ADHD traits shine through despite his serious and calculating demeanor.
